title: Stack Scout // Updates
summary: Public-safe activity stream seeded from official or first-party sources.

items.title: Research agenda proposes seven open problems for multi-agent AI swarms
items.summary: A JinesisLab researcher says each problem is scored for its importance to AI alignment.

items.title: Eight-video course on building reasoning models is online
items.summary: Sebastian Raschka says the course offers over 11 hours of Python and PyTorch coding on evaluation, reinforcement learning and distillation.

items.title: Shigeru Miyamoto selected for Japan's Order of Culture, reflects on AI and creativity
items.summary: Famitsu reports Miyamoto distinguished creating from the satisfying work of execution, saying AI could make that difference clearer.

items.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’
items.summary: The footage looks okay, as long as you're not seeking artistry, inspiration, or human interest.

items.title: One-time reset restores 25% of monthly quota for Kimi subscribers
items.summary: Kimi apologized for K3.1 Pro rate limits and unnecessary quota use, saying it is reducing unnecessary subagent calls.

items.title: Softmax and cross-entropy implementations reportedly contain two subtle bugs
items.summary: On X, @jon_barron claims a simple rewrite fixes both bugs and eliminates slingshots during grokking.

items.title: @theo's T3 Code work list includes two-click clones and live guest thread sharing
items.summary: In an October 25 post, @theo also described compiler projects and put other merged PRs at roughly 370.

items.title: A musical joke about rain on a wedding day
items.summary: A poster riffs on “It's like raaaaain on your wedding day” and links to a photo.

items.title: The 'Scale mafia' and its alumni in AI, venture capital and government
items.summary: Alexandr Wang calls Scale alumni the 'first true mafia of the modern tech era,' listing their current roles.

items.title: AI delivers ‘zero financial payoff’ to most companies, Apollo economist says
items.summary: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech."

items.title: The hottest AI wearables and gadgets you should know about
items.summary: We compiled a list of all the hottest AI wearables, including Muse Charm, Bee, Friend, Plaud, and more.

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.

items.title: Block’s new voice model sounds eerily human
items.summary: Block said that the voice model can run locally on a MacBook M4 Max

items.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
items.summary: A new study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommends Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats, with the two AI models disagreeing in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.

items.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.summary: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.

items.title: Make opened its CLI to all users
items.summary: Make's 2026 release notes show the Make CLI becoming available to all users, continuing the platform's expansion beyond the browser UI.

items.title: GitHub MCP Server reached 1.0.0
items.summary: The official GitHub MCP server hit 1.0.0 with granular issue field tooling and broader MCP Apps support behind feature flags.

items.title: GitHub CLI 2.90.0 introduced `gh skill` in public preview
items.summary: The latest GitHub CLI release adds search, install, preview, update, and publish flows for portable agent skills.

items.title: Hugging Face added Kernels to the Hub
items.summary: The Hub changelog added Kernels as a new way to browse precompiled, hardware-specific kernels and also continues to push agent traces into the product story.

items.title: Strudel Studio's latest public pass focused on smoke-run reliability
items.summary: The recent manager-side pass caught and fixed a release-smoke issue while keeping the studio workflow moving forward.

items.title: Canvas Planner stayed clean and review-ready in its latest public pass
items.summary: The latest public-ready manager pass kept the board surface fast and uncluttered while tightening browser behavior.

items.title: Playwright MCP 0.0.70 landed as the latest maintenance release
items.summary: The current tagged release is a maintenance cut, while the docs continue to push Playwright MCP as a first-class browser layer for agent workflows.

items.title: n8n kept its March 2026 release line moving
items.summary: The March release notes show continued 1.12x shipping, while docs and blog updates highlight secrets-provider and workflow-hardening work.

items.title: OpenAI launched GPT-5.4
items.summary: GPT-5.4 arrived with native computer use, tool search, and 1M-token context, reinforcing OpenAI's focus on real agent workflows.

items.title: Perplexity doubled down on its product thesis in March 2026
items.summary: Perplexity's public blog framed 'The AI is the Computer' and kept tying that story to its API and device ambitions from late February.

items.title: Anthropic's current system-card set centers Claude Sonnet 4.6
items.summary: Anthropic's model materials list Claude Sonnet 4.6 as the current Sonnet generation and explicitly note API access among the active surfaces.

items.title: Wrangler 4.58.0 improved command grouping and auth ergonomics
items.summary: Cloudflare's Workers SDK release added grouped help categories, better auth token retrieval, and type generation on dev startup.
